output.summary: A perennial sedge native to North America, North Asia and Europe, common cottongrass grows in bogs and other open wetlands, often on peat or acidic soil. Its small brown-green flowers develop conspicuous white, cotton-like seed heads in early summer.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds and stems are used in traditional Alaska Native, Inuit and Inupiat cooking; leaves and roots are also described as edible.
